literal.prompt: Кто возглавлял монгольское вторжение в русские земли в 1237–1240 годах?

literalGroups.primaryGround: The Pravenc article assigns the western expedition to Batu (L21), says the main force led by Batu was to invade Northeastern Rus while Mönke led a separate southern steppe force (L27), and describes Batu's 1237 invasion (L29). Alexander's and Ivan III's records place their documented actions in other episodes and periods. This establishes one key while keeping the alternatives historically plausible.
literalGroups.locator: Pravenc L21, L27-L29; Alexander PRlib L44-L51; Ivan III PRlib L44-L48.

literalGroups.literal: На курултае 1235 года царевичу Батыю поручили поход против Руси и других земель. В 1237 году его основное войско вторглось в Северо-Восточную Русь; Мункэ командовал другим направлением.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The source says the 1235 expedition was assigned to Batu and the main force under him invaded Northeastern Rus in 1237; it assigns Mönke a separate direction.

literalGroups.literal: Батый был одним из старших сыновей Джучи.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The article identifies Batu as one of Jochi's older sons, adding an own-option genealogical fact beyond the prompt and key.

literalGroups.literal: Мункэ командовал частью войск, направленной против аланов и половцев в южнорусских степях.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The article assigns Mönke a separate force against the Alans and Polovtsians in the southern Russian steppes.

literalGroups.literal: Александр Невский победил шведов на Неве и рыцарей на Чудском озере.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The Presidential Library article describes Alexander Nevsky’s victories over the Swedes at the Neva and the German knights at Lake Peipus, the own-option fact retained in this note.

literalGroups.literal: Иван III расширил Московское государство и противостоял Орде на реке Угре.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The Ivan III Presidential Library biography describes his expansion of the Moscow state (L49); the retained Ugra article describes his opposition to the Horde there in 1480 (L43-L48). Together these support the original note.
literalGroups.locator: Ivan III PRlib L49, L57; Ugra PRlib L43-L48.

absoluteDifficulty.audienceGround: For adults familiar with Russian history, Batu's leadership of the 1237 invasion is a recognizable thematic fact. Mönke is a plausible contemporary Mongol commander; Alexander Nevsky and Ivan III are recognizable rulers connected with Rus and the Horde. An adult outside the topic can narrow the choices but cannot infer the key from an absurd or grammatically marked alternative.
